Toy stochastic character map of elevation states

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_simmap_elevation.Rd

Stochastic character map (simmap) of phylograftR::toy_backbone with two elevation states, "high" and "low", to combine with phylograftR::toy_simmap (color) or phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges (biogeographic ranges) as examples of attribute-based constraints applied on two traits at once.

It was simulated with phytools::sim.history() from a root in state "low", with equal transition rates between the two states (0.04 per unit of time). Among the first 1000 seeds, the one used (94) is the first giving a map that is balanced and compatible with the constraints of phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits used with phylograftR::toy_simmap (at least one branch in the allowed states of each taxon):

  • The two states cover similar shares of the total branch length (54% "low" and 46% "high").

  • A moderate number of transitions: 12 changes of state, along 9 of the 58 branches (no branch has more than 4 pieces).

  • "high" is found in 18 of the 30 tips and "low" in 12.

Usage

data(toy_simmap_elevation)

Format

An object of classes "simmap" and "phylo" (see phytools::make.simmap()), with the same tips, topology and branch lengths as phylograftR::toy_backbone, and the additional elements $maps (for each branch, the duration spent in each state, from the rootward node to the tipward node), $mapped.edge (total duration per state and branch), $node.states and $states (states of the nodes and tips).

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap for the stochastic character map of colors.

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits for the list of missing taxa to graft, with allowed states of colors and elevation.

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation for the list of missing taxa to graft, with allowed ranges and elevation.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa within a target clade based on elevation, using this dataset.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_simmap_elevation)

# Plot the map
plot(toy_simmap_elevation, colors = c(high = "darkorange", low = "steelblue"),
     fsize = 0.7, ftype = "i")


# Duration spent in each state (sum on all the branches)
colSums(toy_simmap_elevation$mapped.edge)
#>      low     high 
#> 131.1994 110.8468
